questions.question: Rate your proficiency in legal research (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in legal writing (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in contract management (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in reviewing contracts (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in compliance management (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in regulatory research (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in identifying legal and compliance risks (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in developing and reviewing organizational policies (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in preparing legal and compliance documentation (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in legal or commercial due diligence (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in corporate governance concepts (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in privacy and data-protection compliance (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in compliance audits and assessments (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in regulatory compliance (1–10).
Rate your proficiency in managing legal or compliance issues (1–10).
How many projects, assignments, cases, or real work experiences have you completed involving legal research?
How many projects or real work experiences have you completed involving contract review or contract management?
How many projects or real work experiences have you completed involving compliance or regulatory work?
How many projects, cases, or real work experiences have you completed involving legal or compliance risk analysis?
How many projects or real work experiences have you completed involving due diligence, governance, or related legal review?
Briefly describe one legal, compliance, contract, regulatory, or governance project you completed.
How much of the work did you complete yourself versus with a team?
How much did you rely on AI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot while completing the work?
What was the hardest legal or compliance problem you encountered?
How confident are you explaining the sources, reasoning, risks, and final recommendation to someone else?
What is the primary purpose of legal research?

options.A: Identify and evaluate relevant legal authorities for a particular issue
options.B: Find any source that supports the preferred conclusion

questions.question: When evaluating a legal source, why is jurisdiction important?

options.A: The authority's relevance and binding effect can depend on the jurisdiction involved
options.C: Jurisdiction never matters in legal research
options.D: Jurisdiction determines the font used in the decision

questions.question: A researcher finds an old case that supports a conclusion. What should be checked?

options.A: Whether it remains valid and how later authorities have treated it
options.C: Only the date it was published
options.D: Whether the opinion is visually well formatted

questions.question: What is a primary authority generally?

options.A: A source such as legislation, regulations, or judicial decisions that itself carries legal authority

questions.question: Why should legal researchers distinguish binding from persuasive authority?

options.A: They have different levels of legal force in a given context
options.D: Binding authority can never be challenged

questions.question: A statute appears relevant to an issue, but an exception may apply. What should the researcher do?

options.A: Read the relevant provisions, definitions, exceptions, and related authorities carefully

questions.question: Why is precise issue-spotting important?

options.A: The applicable law can depend on the specific facts and legal question being analyzed
options.B: Every legal issue has the same rule
options.C: It reduces the need for sources

questions.question: A secondary source cites a case, but the researcher needs to rely on the case itself. What should they do?

options.A: Locate and review the underlying authority

questions.question: Why is citation accuracy important in legal research?

options.A: It allows others to locate and verify the authority supporting the analysis
options.B: It makes a legal argument automatically correct
options.D: It eliminates the need for primary sources

questions.question: A student claims substantial legal-research experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The legal issue, research strategy, authorities considered, how validity was checked, and how the authorities supported the conclusion
options.C: Only the number of cases found

questions.question: What should a contract reviewer pay particular attention to?

options.A: Rights, obligations, definitions, conditions, deadlines, risks, and remedies

questions.question: A contract contains a payment clause that conflicts with another section. What should the reviewer do?

options.A: Identify and resolve the inconsistency before treating the terms as clear

questions.question: What is contract management primarily concerned with after a contract is signed?

options.A: Tracking obligations, milestones, changes, risks, and performance
options.D: Avoiding communication with the other party

questions.question: Why are defined terms important in contracts?

options.A: They establish specific meanings used throughout the agreement

questions.question: A vendor misses a contractual milestone. What should contract management review first?

options.A: The relevant obligation, deadline, notice requirements, and available remedies

questions.question: Why are termination provisions important?

options.A: They establish circumstances and procedures under which the agreement may end
options.B: They guarantee the contract will end

questions.question: A contract requires written notice for certain changes. A team member makes the change informally. What is the concern?

options.A: The required contractual process may not have been followed

questions.question: Why maintain a contract-obligation tracker?

options.A: It helps monitor responsibilities, dates, deliverables, and compliance

questions.question: A proposed limitation-of-liability clause is unusually broad. What should a reviewer consider?

options.A: Scope, risk allocation, exceptions, and the consequences for the organization

questions.question: A student claims real contract-review experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they identified material obligations, risks, inconsistencies, commercial points, and follow-up actions

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a compliance program?

options.A: Help an organization identify, manage, and monitor applicable legal or regulatory obligations
options.B: Guarantee that violations can never occur

questions.question: A new regulation may affect a company's operations. What should compliance staff determine first?

options.A: Whether and how the rule applies to the organization's activities and obligations
options.C: Ignore the regulation until an audit

questions.question: Why should compliance obligations be mapped to responsible owners?

options.A: Clear ownership supports accountability and monitoring
options.C: It removes the need for policies

questions.question: A regulation has been amended. What should a compliance team do?

options.A: Assess the changes, affected obligations, and required updates
options.B: Continue using the old interpretation automatically

questions.question: Why are compliance controls documented?

options.A: To establish how obligations are operationally addressed and monitored
options.D: To guarantee there will be no violations

questions.question: A business operates across multiple jurisdictions. Why might compliance requirements differ?

options.A: Different jurisdictions can impose different legal and regulatory obligations

questions.question: A control exists on paper but employees do not actually follow it. What does this indicate?

options.A: A potential gap between documented controls and operational compliance

questions.question: Why should regulatory research use authoritative sources wherever possible?

options.A: They provide a stronger basis for determining applicable requirements
options.B: All online summaries are equally authoritative
options.C: Secondary summaries always override primary rules
options.D: Authoritative sources are only needed after a violation

questions.question: A compliance requirement has no identified internal owner. What is the main risk?

options.A: The obligation may not be consistently implemented or monitored

questions.question: A student claims real compliance experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The requirement, applicable source, affected process, controls, owner, monitoring, and gaps identified

questions.question: What is the purpose of legal or compliance risk assessment?

options.A: Identify potential legal or regulatory exposures and evaluate their significance

questions.question: A compliance risk is both highly likely and potentially severe. What should generally happen?

options.A: Prioritize mitigation and monitoring
options.B: Ignore it because it has not happened yet
options.C: Remove it from the risk register

questions.question: A contract contains an obligation the organization may not be able to meet. What should be considered?

options.A: Feasibility, consequences, alternatives, and possible contractual changes
options.D: Assume the other party will waive it

questions.question: A business collects more personal information than it appears to need. What should compliance consider?

options.A: Whether the collection is necessary, authorized, appropriately protected, and consistent with applicable requirements
options.B: Collect more data to be safe

questions.question: Why should risk assessments include both likelihood and impact?

options.A: A risk's priority depends on both how likely it is and how serious the consequences could be
options.B: Likelihood is the only factor that matters

questions.question: A legal issue can affect several business functions. What should the organization consider?

options.A: The cross-functional impact and coordination required to manage the risk

questions.question: A control reduces risk but is not tested regularly. What is the concern?

options.A: The organization may not know whether the control continues to operate effectively

questions.question: What is a risk register useful for?

options.A: Track identified risks, owners, ratings, responses, and status

questions.question: A new business arrangement creates an unfamiliar legal exposure. What is appropriate?

options.A: Assess the issue using relevant law, facts, controls, and expert input where required
options.B: Assume it is acceptable because the business opportunity is large
options.C: Ignore it until a dispute occurs

questions.question: A student claims legal-risk assessment experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The issue, applicable requirements, risk assessment, controls, mitigation, stakeholders, and remaining exposure

questions.question: Why should access to sensitive personal data be restricted?

options.A: To reduce unauthorized access and use
options.B: To make information harder for authorized users to use
options.D: To guarantee there can never be a breach

questions.question: An organization collects personal data for a defined purpose. Why should it avoid unnecessary collection?

options.A: Excessive collection can create additional privacy and compliance risk
options.D: Personal data has no compliance implications

questions.question: What makes an internal compliance policy useful?

options.A: It clearly defines expected behavior, responsibilities, procedures, and escalation where relevant
options.B: It contains broad statements without ownership

questions.question: A policy conflicts with a newly applicable regulation. What should happen?

options.A: Review and update the policy to align with the applicable requirement

questions.question: What is corporate governance primarily concerned with?

options.A: Oversight, accountability, decision rights, controls, and responsible organizational management

questions.question: Why is clear decision authority important in governance?

options.A: It establishes who can make, approve, or oversee important decisions
options.D: It removes the need for policies

questions.question: A staff member wants to export sensitive data to a personal device to work from home. What should they consider first?

options.A: Whether the transfer is authorized and complies with applicable security and privacy requirements
options.C: Whether the employee has enough storage

questions.question: Why should policies be communicated and trained?

options.A: Employees need to understand the expected behavior and how to follow the policy
options.D: Policies should remain unknown to employees

questions.question: A compliance committee receives reports but has no defined authority or follow-up process. What is the concern?

options.A: Governance responsibilities and accountability may be unclear
options.B: More reports will solve the problem automatically

questions.question: A student claims practical governance or privacy-compliance experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The requirement, policy or control, responsibilities, data or decision flows, monitoring, and issues handled

questions.question: What is the purpose of due diligence?

options.A: Investigate relevant facts, risks, obligations, and other material considerations before a decision

questions.question: A potential business partner refuses to provide important compliance documentation. What should be considered?

options.A: The missing information as a potential risk requiring further investigation or escalation

questions.question: What is the purpose of a compliance audit?

options.A: Assess whether relevant controls or practices meet applicable requirements and internal standards
options.B: Guarantee there are no future violations

questions.question: An audit finds that a required control is not operating consistently. What should follow?

options.A: Document the finding, assess its significance, identify corrective action, and monitor remediation
options.C: Ignore it if no incident occurred

questions.question: Why should legal documentation clearly identify relevant dates, parties, obligations, and sources where applicable?

options.A: Clear documentation supports accuracy, traceability, and review

questions.question: A compliance audit sample shows several failures. What should the auditor consider?

options.A: Whether the pattern indicates a broader control problem and requires expanded testing
options.C: Assume the remaining population is compliant

questions.question: A due-diligence review finds a material contractual obligation that was not previously disclosed. What should happen?

options.A: Assess its legal, financial, operational, and commercial impact before proceeding
options.B: Ignore it because it was discovered late

questions.question: A legal memo reaches a conclusion but does not explain the supporting authorities. What is the main weakness?

options.A: The reasoning cannot be properly evaluated or verified from the document
options.D: More formatting is the only fix

questions.question: After corrective actions are implemented, why should remediation be retested?

options.A: To determine whether the corrective action actually addressed the identified gap

questions.question: A student claims substantial legal/compliance experience. Which question best verifies genuine practical experience?

options.A: Ask them to walk through a real matter from issue identification and research through risk assessment, documentation, stakeholder handling, and final recommendation
options.B: Ask only which legal database they used
options.C: Ask only how many documents they reviewed
options.D: Ask only which organization they worked for
